by PR #767. Identify DML at the start of the query string (first word match).
Update get_query_plan() to branch on DML vs. SELECT. For DML, omit ANALYZE and

description:
PostgreSQLAdapter.get_query_plan() at benchbox/platforms/postgresql.py:704 always
issues EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON). PostgreSQL's EXPLAIN ANALYZE
physically re-executes the target query to collect actual timing and row counts.
For DML statements — INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, COPY — this causes the
write to execute twice: once during the timed benchmark phase and once again
during plan capture. There is no DML guard today.

This violates the hard requirement that plan capture must not cause write
side-effects on the measured data set. DML double-execution corrupts benchmark
data (row counts, aggregations, sequence values) in ways that are difficult to
detect and reproduce.

DuckDB already has this guard: PR #767
(fix/plan-capture): guard DuckDB/MotherDuck DML against double-execution.
The fix there detects DML and falls back to EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) (no ANALYZE)
which produces an estimated plan without re-executing. PostgreSQL supports the
same fallback: EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) is valid PostgreSQL syntax and returns a
JSON plan tree without ANALYZE overhead.

Scope: PostgreSQLAdapter only. TimescaleDB, CedarDB, and pg_mooncake inherit
get_query_plan() from PostgreSQLAdapter and will receive the fix for free.
RedshiftAdapter.get_query_plan() issues plain EXPLAIN (no ANALYZE) already, so
it is not affected.

Note: the `query-plan-capture-dml-double-execution` TODO (if it exists) may
have been authored with the incorrect assumption that PostgreSQL already uses
FORMAT JSON without ANALYZE. This item supersedes that assumption — the actual
code at postgresql.py:704 uses ANALYZE.

anti_patterns.dont: add a DML guard to RedshiftAdapter
anti_patterns.why: it already uses plain EXPLAIN without ANALYZE.

anti_patterns.dont: add the guard to the base class
anti_patterns.why: the guard logic is PostgreSQL-specific; other adapters have different EXPLAIN semantics.

anti_patterns.dont: parse the full query AST to detect DML
anti_patterns.why: first-word detection is sufficient and robust enough for plan capture purposes.
actual timing is required for meaningful plan analysis.

preserves.behavior: EXPLAIN ANALYZE (the current default for SELECT) must remain unchanged — DML-only guard.
Plan capture failures must remain non-fatal when strict_plan_capture is False (the default).
PostgreSQLQueryPlanParser must be able to parse the non-ANALYZE fallback path output.
TimescaleDB, CedarDB, and pg_mooncake adapters must not require code changes.
